question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is structuring a new Cat II AIF at GIFT IFSC to attract foreign LPs. Which of the following MOST accurately captures the tax advantages available for a Cat I/II AIF set up in IFSC-GIFT compared to an onshore (non-IFSC) Cat I/II AIF?

answer.text: No tax benefit — IFSC funds are taxed identically to onshore AIFs.
IFSC funds pay a flat 5% tax on all income.
IFSC funds are exempt from SEBI AIF Regulations.
IFSC funds enjoy a 100% tax holiday on business income for any 10 consecutive years out of 15 (Section 80LA), and management fees from non-resident LPs are zero-rated / exempt from GST.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** A Cat I/II AIF located in IFSC-GIFT (regulated by IFSCA under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022) qualifies for Section 80LA benefits — a 100% deduction for any 10 consecutive years out of 15 on its business income. In addition, investment management services rendered by an IFSC-based manager to non-resident LPs are zero-rated under GST (exports of services). Section 10(23FBA) pass-through continues to apply. This bundle makes IFSC highly competitive with Singapore / Mauritius for fund domicile. **The Trap:** Option A ignores the explicit tax-holiday regime. Option C invents a rate that doesn't exist. Option D is wrong — IFSC funds ARE regulated (by IFSCA), just under a different rulebook than SEBI. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C highlights IFSC-GIFT benefits. XIX-E (Cat III) will test the same for offshore hedge-style funds. Compared to Mauritius Cat 1 GBC, IFSC offers similar tax efficiency plus Indian-jurisdiction regulatory comfort — a selling point to Indian GPs setting up offshore sleeves. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a debt-focused Cat II fund targeting US/EU pension LPs, benchmarking IFSC vs Singapore VCC: IFSC wins on tax holiday, rupee proximity, and IFSCA speed-to-licence. Singapore wins on legal-system maturity. Model both and present to your anchor LP before selecting domicile.
